papers.title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining with Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection for Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
papers.abs: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.

papers.title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
papers.abs: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. papers.title: Thouless Pumping of One-Dimensional Dark Solitons and Domain Walls
papers.abs: We predict that quantized transport of dark solitons and domain walls can be observed in mutually sliding optical lattices in both focusing and defocusing nonlinear materials. Two different classes of underlying periodic backgrounds are considered here -- unstaggered and staggered -- which are accurately represented, respectively, by the in-phase and out-of-phase trains of Wannier functions. The nonlinear excitations formed on top of these backgrounds -- dark solitons and domain walls -- are sustained by defocusing or focusing Kerr nonlinearities of the optical medium. Despite non-zero asymptotics, dark solitons and domain walls can still undergo quantized topological transport in dynamically changing refractive index landscape when they and background on which they are constructed are dynamically stable. The extended intervals of propagation constants (and, correspondingly, of the background amplitude) and lattice depths, where stable quantized transport occurs, are identified for both dark solitons and domain walls. Laser with $7\times10^{-18}$ stability
papers.abs: We report a laser with record frequency stability, based on a 21 cm cryogenic silicon cavity. For best short-term stability, the cavity operates at 6 K to minimize Brownian thermal noise and achieves a fractional stability of $7\times10^{-18}$ between 2 to 50 s of averaging time and 2.5 mHz linewidth. For best long-term stability the cavity operates at 16 K, where silicon has a zero-crossing of thermal expansion. Slightly increased thermal noise limits the performance to $9\times10^{-18}$, consistent with the expected temperature scaling, but the long-term performance is improved. The laser then has a linewidth of 2.9 mHz and long-term frequency drift less than 4 μHz s$^{-1}$. The laser is used to enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art Sr lattice clock, operating with Rabi and Ramsey interrogation times beyond 10 s.

papers.abs: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. papers.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
papers.abs: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. papers.title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
papers.abs: Objective: To develop a unified and efficient method for projection-domain material decomposition in spectral computed tomography (CT) that incorporates an arbitrary number of spectral measurements, independent of the acquisition mechanism, without reducing the measurements to two effective energies. Approach: A nested optimization method was developed for two-material basis decomposition from K>=2 spectral measurements. It extends an existing two-measurement univariate method by replacing its polynomial approximation with profile minimization of the Poisson negative log-likelihood, reducing the inversion to two one-dimensional searches that use all measurements without spectral rebinning. The method was evaluated in simulation for energy-integrating (GE Revolution Apex Elite, Siemens SOMATOM Flash) and photon-counting (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) CT. Main results: The method recovered line integrals with noiseless iodine errors below 3e-6 g/cm^2 and noise within 3% of the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). papers.abs: Multiplexed optical biosensors are widely deployed to read out many biological targets in parallel. However, their channel count and integration density are limited by the photonic network that delivers light to individual sensing sites. Existing on-chip networks have been largely developed for phased arrays and image projection, where performance is assessed through an aggregate radiation pattern rather than the local intensity at each output. Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
papers.abs: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.

papers.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
papers.abs: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. papers.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
papers.abs: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mech

papers.title: Pure dephasing destroys two-photon amplitude, not nonlinear phase
papers.abs: A two-level emitter chirally coupled to a waveguide imprints a $π$ conditional phase on a two-photon pulse, a key component assumed in quantum photonic neural network architectures, but whether it survives the pure dephasing of a solid-state emitter is unknown, since no two-photon scattering treatment includes it. We derive the dephased two-photon amplitude in closed form and validate it against an independent Fock-state master equation. The conditional phase is pinned at exactly $π$ at every dephasing rate examined: dephasing destroys the amplitude carrying the nonlinear phase rather than rotating it. The one- and two-photon channels are not attenuated equally, so dephasing does not simply scale the node down but reweights it between photon-number sectors---an error no phase setting can train away. The standard factorization of two-photon correlators, exact for arbitrary loss, fails at first order in $γ_φ$, discarding $16$--$81\%$ of pairs over $γ_φ/γ=0.1$--$1$.

Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
papers.abs: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI): an effective saturable absorber built from cascaded second-order nonlinearity in periodically poled lithium niobate nanophotonics, with a measured sub-20 fs response time. papers.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
papers.abs: Majorana drew a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the Bloch sphere, antipodal to the zeros of its overlap with spin coherent states. Projecting only one qubit of a general state leaves the others in a state that varies with direction. Its entanglement invariants are eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix and form bands over the sphere. Exceptional points appear, without gain or loss, where the entanglement family of the rest changes. Circling one exchanges two bands, so the bands form one Riemann surface. At five qubits it fixes the entanglement class up to finitely many choices.

UNWRAP: Single-shot phase analysis of bright squeezed vacuum by Newton-ring interferometry
papers.abs: The mean field of pulsed bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) vanishes, but the variance can be large, and is strongly phase-dependent. We employ ultrafast Newton-ring wavefront retrieval and analysis of phase (UNWRAP) to extract the field amplitude and phase profile of each BSV pulse, by Fourier analysis of the interference rings between the BSV and a coherent reference with different phase-front curvature. The concentric ring interference fringes are robust against pointing mismatch and drift, thereby simplifying the analysis. The measured distribution has two phase peaks separated by π radians. The rings sweep the delay between the two pulses, so a single frame can capture the temporal field profile of the BSV, even when it is composed of several temporal modes.

Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$
papers.abs: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. Meta-optics offer a compact, lightweight, and potentially low-cost alternative to conventional refractive optics, making them attractive for size, weight, and power (SWaP)-constrained systems. Remarkably, the reconstruction model is adapted using only four image captures, overcoming large training data requirements and enabling broadband image recovery despite the strongly wavelength-dependent optical response. Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
papers.abs: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. papers.abs: We study the nonlinear dynamics of spinor exciton-polaritons in resonantly pumped microcavities. Using steady-state analysis and computing eigenfrequencies via Bogoliubov-like linearization, we show that multiple Hopf bifurcations beyond conventional bistability occur within specific power regimes and are not associated with stable solutions of the system. Owing to nonlinear excitonic interactions, these transitions occur at different pump powers during forward and backward pump sweeps, leading to pronounced hysteresis between fixed-point and limit-cycle states. In the spinor regime, multiple limit-cycle branches and associated dynamical hysteresis loops emerge due to the interplay of polarization coupling and spin-dependent nonlinearities. We show how the locations of the bifurcation points can be tuned by the pump frequency and other system parameters. Our results identify synchronization as the organizing principle underlying limit-cycle formation, dynamical hysteresis, and bifurcation cascades in driven spinor exciton-polariton microcavities.

papers.abs: Adaptive optics (AO) corrected image restoration is particularly difficult, as it suffers from the lack of knowledge on the point spread function (PSF) in addition to usual difficulties. An efficient approach is to marginalize the object out of the problem and to estimate the PSF and (object and noise) hyperparameters only, before deconvolving the object using these estimates. Recent works have applied this marginal blind deconvolution method, combined to a parametric model of the PSF, to a series of AO corrected astronomical and satellite images. In this communication, we propose a new restoration method, which consists in choosing the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimator and computing the latter thanks to a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm. We validate our method by means of realistic simulations, in two very different contexts: an astronomical observation on VLT/SPHERE and a ground-based LEO satellite observation on a 1.52m telescope. Finally, we present results on experimental images for both applications.

papers.abs: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. papers.abs: Optically addressable electron spin qubits that function at room temperature and under ambient conditions are essential for advancing quantum sensing. These defects were shown to emit in the near infrared within the biological transparency window, and their placement on the nanotube surface provides nanoscale proximity to target environments. papers.title: Two-dimensional structures formed by pair potentials: An analytical and numerical study
papers.abs: Understanding the thickness dependence of the excess energy of thin films and identifying the deviation from the scaling law that holds for thicker films are crucial for predicting the formation of two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from nonlayered structures, commonly referred to as non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials. Here, we analytically study the excess energy of thin films as a function of the number of layers $N$, assuming pair potentials. We show that the $1/N$ scaling law of the excess energy breaks down in the monolayer limit when the interatomic interactions are long-ranged. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations using the Lennard-Jones and Morse potentials. The present work suggests that non-vdW 2D structures can be formed by pair potentials alone.

papers.abs: Thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising integrated photonic platform owing to its large quadratic nonlinearity enabling vital applications such as second-harmonic generation (SHG), optical parametric amplification, and spontaneous parametric down-conversion. However, to achieve high SH conversion efficiency, quasi-phase matching (QPM) through periodic electrical poling is typically required, which remains challenging in certain applications like multiple-ring coupled devices. Here, we demonstrate a surface molecule patterning strategy to enable QPM in a poling-free TFLN microring for SHG. An on-chip normalized conversion efficiency of approximately 11.5%/W is obtained in the poling-free TFLN microring with surface molecular pattern, showing an approximate 400-fold improvement compared to the same microring without surface molecular pattern. This approach offers a versatile route to engineer interfacial nonlinear interactions for nonlinear optics and quantum photonics applications and may be extended to multiple-ring coupled resonators and other platforms.

papers.abs: Symmetries play a crucial role in protecting the topological phases of insulators, ensuring the robustness of their surface states against perturbations. Traditionally, these symmetries have to be obeyed by the system as a whole, which is a rather strong constraint. In this work, we demonstrate that topological effects can also be realized through a substantially weaker form of symmetry that we coin \emph{partial latent symmetries}. These weak-symmetry models behave in many aspects just like their conventional brethren---in particular, they host robust edge states---, though the corresponding topological invariants are only \emph{approximately} quantized. papers.title: Characterizing universal topological phases beyond spatial embedding
papers.abs: Although Hamiltonians govern wave-matter interactions, conventional characterizations of topological phases of matter require more than the Hamiltonian alone, relying on global invariants defined on closed reciprocal-space manifolds or local commutation relations with position operators. This spatial dependence precludes a unique characterization of topological phases on an abstract platform, whose Hamiltonian can be defined independently of its spatial embedding. Here we establish a framework for characterizing universal topological phases, grounded in the invariance of topological features under arbitrary Hamiltonian-preserving deformations. We construct a Hamiltonian-based spatial embedding that groups a system's constituents according to their connectivity. papers.title: Optimized Bragg Grating Liquid Crystal Solar Sail
papers.abs: We have designed a thin 3-layer sun-facing diffractive Bragg reflector comprised of a chiral polymeric liquid crystal film. Using Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA), the stack was optimized to maximize the transverse radiation pressure force across the wavelength band 0.47 - 1.67 micrometers. The optimized structure operates on a single polarization state of light. A two structure stack, each operating on a different state of polarization, is predicted to provide a transverse momentum transfer efficiency of 51%. This study demonstrates how a wavelength selective Bragg grating may be used both as a sunshade to scatter sunlight away from the Earth, and as a solar sail for maintaining a prescribed orbit (such as the Earth-Sun L1 point) owing to the momentum transfer efficiency.

With $C=0$ on the wall of a closed perfectly conducting waveguide, the classical modes are unchanged. The SL modes have $\mathbf{B}=0$ and an electric field along $\nabla C$, and their cutoffs are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the cross-section, the same as the TM cutoffs, with no coaxial TEM counterpart. Charge-conserving sources with zero scalar data do not excite them. Matching at a conductor described by its constitutive laws gives $\partial C/\partial n=0$ instead and couples the scalar-bearing modes to the Maxwell field. The results belong to the $C=0$ problem, the condition that separates the sectors and the one divergence cleaning uses, with benchmarks for the rectangular, circular cylinder, coaxial and L-shaped guides.

papers.abs: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI$_2$ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic exciton transport and highlight the critical role of interface protection in air-sensitive van der Waals materials.

Writing the lens body at coarse resolution and the optical surface at fine resolution reduces the print time from 9 h to 19 min per lens. papers.abs: Conventional visual sensing faces a fundamental dilemma: information that should remain private today may need to be recovered tomorrow. This challenge is becoming increasingly important as cameras become pervasive in our daily surroundings. Existing safeguards either protect visual content only after an image is formed or suppress information during capture in ways that prevent its later recovery. Here, we show through an information-theoretic analysis that privacy and recoverability cannot be achieved simultaneously in static optical systems. Information preserved in a measurement for later reconstruction also remains available to an observer of that measurement, limiting the privacy such systems can provide. To overcome this limitation, we introduce conditional imaging, an imaging approach that changes the optical state for every captured frame. papers.abs: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. papers.title: Differentiable powder X-ray diffraction enables analysis of evolving structures
papers.abs: Operando and in-situ experiments extend powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to materials that evolve during experiments, producing series of hundreds or thousands of patterns. Such series are commonly refined one pattern at a time, so weak signals give noisy structural trajectories. Parametric refinement instead fits a shared model to all patterns, but with most existing programs, changing the model or fitting it efficiently remains challenging. Here, we introduce diffPXRD, a differentiable PXRD engine in PyTorch. diffPXRD calculates derivatives by automatic differentiation, so a shared model can be changed without new derivative code. Batched fitting is also more than seven times faster than serial fitting. In an operando cathode series, a shared lattice model can reduce lattice-parameter variability by 68.4% when 10% of the photon counts are retained. We also show shared models can describe the precipitation and dissolution of Li2S and reconstruct collective atomic displacements in Ca3Ti2O7.

papers.abs: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. papers.title: A Solar Optical Clock
papers.abs: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. papers.abs: This paper presents a concept of mechanically adjustable planar Gradientindex (GRIN) lens that can be used to realize reconfigurable focusing at mid-infrared (mid-IR) or millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequencies. Numerical simulations demonstrate accurate focal tuning at mid-IR and mm-waves. In the mid-IR regime, focal lengths of about 56 μm and 24 μm are achieved with relative errors of around 4.4% and 10%, respectively. papers.abs: Structured light provides a route to controlling quantum materials not only through its polarization, but also through its spatial profile and orbital angular momentum (OAM). We develop real space theories of a Weyl semimetal driven by a vortex beam and show that optical OAM generates highly localized Floquet vortex states with pronounced circulating photocurrents. Exploiting cylindrical symmetry, we derive a Bogoliubov-de Gennes-like radial equation that resolves the states by angular momentum and reveals their evolution between the light-dressed Weyl cones. For Laguerre-Gaussian beams, the spatially varying drive produces strong hybridization between localized vortex states and bulk states. We complement this continuum description with a Wilson-lattice formulation that retains the full two-dimensional spatial structure and enables direct calculation of local photocurrents. Both approaches consistently identify OAM-induced vortex states localized around the beam axis. papers.abs: A varifocal mid-infrared metalens designed for focusing applications is proposed to integrate both Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) and Moiré pattern-based mechanisms for rotational wavefront control. papers.abs: Photonic and qubit-based (digital) approaches to quantum computing are largely regarded as separate paradigms. This article aims to bridge these paradigms by developing a method for mapping quantum-optical systems onto qubit-based quantum circuits. The key ingredient enabling this mapping is the introduction of a truncation of the Fock space describing single-mode optical states. Within this framework, representations of basic photonic operations are developed, including the phase-rotation operator, the displacement operator, the squeezing operator, and the beam splitter. Explicit quantum circuit constructions are provided for Fock-space truncations of dimension $N=2$ and $N=4$. We discuss benchmarking of the implemented operations and identify the regime of applicability and the limitations of the proposed method. papers.title: Electronic driving of torsional modes in carbon nanotubes via orbital-phonon coupling
papers.abs: We theoretically investigate electronic driving of a torsional mode in a suspended carbon nanotube quantum dot. The valley states in a nanotube carry opposite orbital magnetic moments along the tube axis, and intervalley mixing forms valley-mixed eigenstates whose splitting can be controlled by an axial magnetic field. We formulate an orbital-rotation coupling between the torsional angular velocity and the valley orbital angular momentum. Using a master equation for sequential tunneling through normal-metal electrodes, we calculate the steady-state current and the phonon distribution of the torsional mode. When the valley-state splitting matches the torsional phonon energy, orbital transitions can drive the mode out of equilibrium. The contacts control both phonon pumping and its electrical readout, allowing substantial excitation with a positive, vanishing, or negative current response. The mechanism requires no intrinsic spin or valley polarization of the electrodes, but uses state-dependent tunneling at the contacts.

papers.title: Dual Transverse Vortex-Spin-Momentum Locking in Rotating-Wave Structured Light
papers.abs: We theoretically investigate the transverse Poynting momentum and transverse spin angular momentum in circularly polarized rotating-wave structured light, and reveal a pair of dual transverse vortex-spin-momentum locking. The transverse Poynting momentum exhibits a $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetric locking structure, being controlled independently by either the polarization or vortex handedness, yet invariant under their simultaneous reversal. Meanwhile, the transverse spin angular momentum is independent of the polarization but endowed with a crucial vortex-dependence inheriting such vortex-dependence from the Poynting momentum via curl operation. This finding expands the understanding of transverse optical linear and angular momenta in structured light and opens a new paradigm for vortex-spin-controlled optical manipulation.

papers.abs: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. papers.abs: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.

papers.title: Atmospheric channel model for QKD over satellite megaconstellations
papers.abs: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. The model is validated with available data from missions such as Micius and Hispasat, including a secondary viability assessment for a hypothetical Starlink-based quantum communication network, where we evaluate the predicted channel behavior in terms of single-photon transmittance and power balance, alongside the channel capacity of the link for uplink and downlink exclusively. Our comparative analysis demonstrates the ability of our channel model to predict real data under simple atmospheric behavior assumptions, which offer practical guidelines for the design and optimization of future quantum satellite missions.

papers.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
papers.abs: Concatenation of quantum repeater nodes has been proposed as a means to distribute entanglement efficiently across future long-distance networks. Here, we demonstrate a trapped-ion repeater node that establishes photonic entanglement over a 17 km fiber traversing a city, moving beyond laboratory-only prototypes. The node comprises two atomic ions coupled to an optical cavity. First, a detailed characterization is performed of the long fiber channel and of ion-photon entanglement distributed across it. Next, a repeater-node protocol is implemented, achieving entanglement between a local photon and a remote photon with a Bell-state fidelity of $81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%$. These results demonstrate that trapped-ion repeater-node technology can operate over existing city-scale fiber infrastructure and represent a step toward distributed quantum repeater networks.

papers.title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
papers.abs: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium. After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level $Λ$ system. This spectral narrowing is associated with the decreasing separation between the two inner dressed states as atomic velocity increases. The transparency window exhibits pronounced direction-dependent transmission, with high forward transmission and strong suppression in the reverse direction. The transparency linewidth and forward-backward probe transmission can be controlled via two independent driving fields, while the central transparency frequency is kept essentially unchanged. The resulting narrowband nonreciprocity supports high forward transmission together with strong suppression in the reverse direction, which is suitable for frequency-selective optical filtering and nonreciprocal optical transmission in thermal atomic media. papers.abs: Symmetry-protected ground-state crossings can produce exact first-order transitions (FOTs) even at finite $N$, in contrast to continuous transitions governed by soft-mode criticality. We establish exact Juddian ground-state crossings for arbitrary finite $N$ in the one- and two-photon anisotropic Dicke models and identify a common two-channel structure: the eigenvalues of the coupling matrix set the local normal-state instability thresholds, whereas its determinant fixes the exact crossing. Despite this common structure, the resulting FOTs have distinct fates determined by the bosonic response. In the one-photon model, the overlap between coherent Juddian branches vanishes in the thermodynamic or infinite frequency-ratio limits, asymptotically suppressing the FOT cusp. In the two-photon model, squeezed Juddian states lose normalizability at spectral collapse, thereby terminating the physical FOT line at finite $N$. papers.abs: Electromagnetic surrogate solvers can accelerate nanophotonic design, but their broader use requires accurate predictions for unseen geometries and material arrangements. papers.abs: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. With a 0.9°-sensitivity for polarization rotations in a 1-second measurement and single-shot capability, the device opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast magneto-optic spectroscopy and at accelerator-based light sources.

Together with strain-selective magnetic responses, this identifies single-$\mathbf{q}$ order in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ over the proposed symmetry-preserving double-$\mathbf{q}$ state. Uniaxial compression along a low-symmetry in-plane direction achieves the domain selection that magnetic-field training could not, revealing the intrinsic field-induced phase boundaries of the dominant domain. These results establish strain as a symmetry-conjugate field for magnetic domains and highlight magnetoelastic coupling as a route to diagnose, manipulate, and potentially tune magnetic states.

papers.abs: Coexistence of classical and quantum light in optical fiber is a key requirement for scalable quantum networks. However, it is fundamentally limited by nonlinear crosstalk from intense classical signals. Hollow-core fiber (HCF), with its intrinsically low optical nonlinearity, offers a promising solution. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the coexistence of polarization-entangled photons with dense wavelength-division multiplexed (DWDM) classical signals with a total launch power of 11.2 dBm, and perform a direct comparison between equal-length single-mode fiber (SMF) and photonic-bandgap-based HCF deployed in a campus network. We observe that HCF suppresses background noise by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to SMF, while preserving high-fidelity entanglement distribution. Our results provide clear experimental evidence of the advantage of HCF and establish its potential as a transmission medium.

papers.title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
papers.abs: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. papers.abs: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.

papers.title: Engineering \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two remote superconducting qubits via a multimode waveguide
papers.abs: Waveguides provide a flexible platform for long-range interactions between superconducting qubits. Here, we study how to engineer the effective \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two qubits via qubit frequency assignments and multimode interference determined by the mode configuration and standing-wave parities of a finite multimode waveguide. For a single-mode waveguide, we find that \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions cannot be simultaneously suppressed to zero and the residual qubit-qubit coupling always exists. For example, the \(XY\) interaction may be suppressed to a negligible level when two qubits and the waveguide mode satisfy the two-photon resonant condition, but the \(ZZ\) interaction cannot be switched off. For multimode configurations within the central dispersive window, the engineered interaction types are very different for odd and even numbers of modes. Even-mode configurations can readily produce strong \(XY\) interactions, whereas odd-mode configurations can strongly suppress the \(XY\) interaction while retaining a finite \(ZZ\) interaction. papers.abs: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.

papers.abs: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. papers.abs: On-chip thermal processing is a key technology for materials discovery across all disciplines of the natural sciences. Here, we present a microfabricated heat-delivery platform that enables reaction-induced localized on-chip annealing up to 1400°C. A buried reactive multilayer combined with a nanometric diffusion barrier provide ultra-fast heating and quenching rates on the order of 10$^6$°C s$^{-1}$ as illustrated by the generation of ultra-high aspect ratio microstructures during rapid-solidification and the stabilization of dopant-free tetragonal zirconia at room temperature. Rapid kinetics also enable the observation of transient states of capillary-driven hole collapse in melts. Our work expands localized high-temperature processing routes and offers a material-independent approach for rapid screening of multidimensional nanomaterials on and off-equilibrium.

papers.abs: Radiation-pressure forces on transmissive optics, including dynamical backaction, are usually computed from the momentum flux of the external fields. We compute the force on a lossless dielectric slab of arbitrary thickness $L_s$ submerged in a dielectric fluid, proceeding from both Lorentz force on its bound charges and from the external momentum fluxes for arbitrary carrier and sideband fields. We treat the surrounding medium through a prescribed linear dielectric response and do not model the accompanying mechanical response of the fluid, including pressure and electrostriction. These two methods both recover the expected force in the limit of a thin reflector, but differ in the more general case by the rate of change of the field momentum stored in the slab. papers.abs: Artificial-intelligence systems face a growing data-movement bottleneck and require higher interconnect bandwidth without a proportional increase in electrical power consumption or the number of laser sources and fibre connections. papers.title: Beyond Fidelity: Resolving Errors in Photonic Seed State Generation
papers.abs: An important aspect of many linear optical quantum computing architectures is probabilistically generating small dual-rail qubit entangled states, or seed states. While many schemes to achieve this have been discovered, attention has been primarily focused on minimizing input resources and maximizing success probability rather than establishing a detailed understanding of linear-optical error performance. We use this framework to identify seed state generators in which destructive many-photon interference prevents detector loss and detector noise from causing a falsely successful heralding event. papers.abs: The establishment of metrics and control of fundamental noise sources in quantum sensing is a long-standing goal in quantum science and technology. We report on the observation of polariton-mediated optical noise in a thermal Rydberg atom vapor and demonstrate its active control and suppression using a radio-frequency field in Rydberg electrometry. papers.title: Spatiotemporal spherical Gaussian pulses
papers.abs: We describe a class of electromagnetic Gaussian modes with spherical spatiotemporal structure that remains invariant during propagation through anomalously dispersive media. The angular profile of the modes is given by spherical harmonics, whose quantization axis can be freely chosen. As a result, the modes support spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum (OAM) configurations with longitudinal and transverse components set by the orientation of the quantization axis. Superpositions of these modes generalize the familiar solution of a chirped pulse that simultaneously focuses and compresses to arbitrary angular structure. The modes are derived through a series of unitary transformations that map the dispersive paraxial wave equation onto a Schrödinger equation with a 3D isotropic harmonic potential. These transformations facilitate the identification of conserved operators for mixed longitudinal and transverse OAM.

papers.abs: Memory capacity and bandwidth are becoming major constraints in neural-network computing, motivating parameter-efficient representations that reduce model storage and data movement. papers.abs: We investigate open-system charging protocols for Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries under direct incoherent pumping. Here we embed resonators in a photonic band-gap vacuum (BgV), a photonic crystal whose band gap plays for photons the role vacuum plays for bound electrons. The BgV localizes each resonance exponentially, so designed short-range couplings define the lattice Hamiltonian. We thereby experimentally realize a faithful Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes Hamiltonian in an all-dielectric photonic crystal, resolving corner resonances and their orbitals in microwave measurements. Unlike the vacuum surrounding electrons, the BgV is itself designable, controlling relative couplings and closed-loop interference through its band dispersion and Bloch modes. papers.abs: Consider several cavity resonators whose resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields are known, and suppose that they are coupled through apertures. papers.abs: Laser amplification kicks off with just a few photons in the cavity, a regime where standard additive Langevin noise cannot capture the real fluctuations. To understand how this amplification begins, we map out a single-mode photon-carrier model that links macroscopic lasers directly into nanolasers. Stationary rate equations reveal that stimulated emission takes over across a tight pump window. In nanolasers, however, spontaneous processes coexist across a much broader range. Because steady-state averages miss the individual events that lead to the macroscopic photon number, we frame the stochastic dynamics around the actual discrete transitions, deriving a state-dependent diffusion approximation. The destruction of an excited carrier concurrent with the generation of a photon creates a negative photon-carrier cross-correlation. \textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer
papers.abs: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.

papers.abs: Three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging based on structured illumination has attracted considerable attention in applications including machine vision, robotics, and computational sensing. However, conventional structured-light systems generally rely on bulky projection components, such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which limit system miniaturization and integration. papers.title: Superradiant temporal transition radiation of a relativistic electron beam
papers.abs: A charge in uniform motion carries a bound field that does not radiate. Transition radiation releases part of it at a boundary in space. We propose and analyze the case of radiation emission due to a boundary in time: a relativistic electron bunch passes through an aperture in a semiconductor (silicon) wafer, and while its bound field occupies the wafer, a femtosecond laser switches the semiconductor into an electron-hole plasma. The field is a valid solution of the old medium and not of the new one, so it is handed to the plasma as an initial condition for radiation emission at the plasma frequency. Because in temporal transition radiation (t-TR) the wavevector is conserved, and the frequency is not, the emission can appear in a spectral band that the bunch's own field does not populate. Every electron contributes in phase to the initial condition at the switching moment, so the emitted energy scales as $N^2$. papers.title: Photon production at Kepler escape threshold
papers.abs: We obtain an exact closed-form total photon count for a prescribed Newtonian Kepler parabola, with a fully relativistic treatment of its radiation. We also obtain closed expressions for the angularly resolved photon spectrum and elementary expressions for the total radiated energy and momenta. The count is finite, scale-independent, and analytic in subluminal speed at closest approach. At large maximum rapidity $η$, $N\sim(7α/\sqrt6)η$, while $E\propto e^{3η}$ at fixed passage timescale: the radiation chiefly hardens. For slow motion at fixed coupling and closest distance, a nearby ellipse emits fewer photons but more energy and angular momentum per orbit. The hyperbolic photon count remains IR divergent arbitrarily close to threshold, while the count at the exact parabolic threshold is finite.

papers.abs: The spatial distribution of energy in silicon thin films under femtosecond laser irradiation is demonstrated to be influenced by the interaction between carrier-induced refractive index modulation and self-induced Fabry-Pérot resonances. Numerical results demonstrate that at higher fluences, plasma-induced extinction suppresses internal reflections, triggering a transition from resonance-mediated absorption to plasma shielding. papers.title: Chiral Floquet Selection of an Algebraic Rydberg Bound State in the Continuum
papers.abs: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain localized despite the presence of extended modes at the same energy. In driven systems with long-range couplings, the absence of radiation does not by itself determine how a bound state decays in space. We study a Hermitian Rydberg spin waveguide coupled to a four-site plaquette, where a winding drive phase combines rotation with time translation to forbid propagating guide channels in one symmetry sector. The resulting eigenstate remains embedded in the continuum of other sectors and carries an inverse-cube waveguide amplitude, with coherent contributions from direct plaquette--guide coupling and long-range guide propagation. Pair-state calculations determine the microscopic couplings in the axial geometry, while coherent Floquet mixing sets the weight of the dominant circulating plaquette mode. The bound state thus retains the spatial signature of the long-range coupling even when radiation is forbidden.

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking chelation enables room-temperature all-optical spin coherence readout of aqueous Cu(II) for chemoselective discrimination
papers.abs: Optical initialization and readout of molecular electron spins in water remains challenging for 3d transition-metal complexes. Their Laporte-forbidden d-d transitions yield weak transition dipole moments, so optical spin detection in aqueous Cu(II) previously required ~1 M concentrations. Here we overcome this constraint through symmetry-breaking chelation. Coordinating Cu(II) with EDTA imposes a non-centrosymmetric ligand field with enhanced metal-ligand covalency, relaxing Laporte restrictions and amplifying d-d transition dipole moments. This design enhances absorption and magnetic circular dichroism by 7.3- and 5.6-fold, enabling ultrafast spin readout down to 100 μM with an apparent dephasing time T2^*~0.54 ns. As a proof-of-concept for selective molecular-spin sensing, histidine addition extends T_2^* to ~0.8 ns in a concentration-dependent manner, whereas glycine produces no measurable effect. These results show that symmetry breaking provides a strategy to create molecular spin-photon interfaces, opening avenues toward all-optical, analyte-responsive quantum sensing in water.

papers.abs: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. papers.abs: Detecting chirality is essential in chemistry and biomedicine. Circular dichroism identifies chiral molecules through their differential absorption of circularly polarized light. papers.abs: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) represents a fundamental degree of freedom (DoF) for understanding novel phenomena in solids and synthetic lattices. However, the generation and control of OAM in lattice systems remain challenging. Here, we experimentally observe valley-controlled OAM states in inversion-symmetry-broken photonic honeycomb lattices consisting of s- and higher-orbital sublattices. papers.abs: At a spatially uniform, in-plane-isotropic time boundary, the transverse displacement of a spatiotemporal optical vortex changes sign with its topological charge, despite a charge-independent conversion weight. In a finite pumped GaAs waveguide, unequal attenuation during extraction adds angular deflection. Independent Maxwell--Drude simulations test this extraction-induced response and give $\pm42$~mrad before detector filtering. papers.abs: Quantum correlation measurements have emerged as a powerful tool for localizing multiple emitters with subwavelength separation. Multi-emitter localization consists of two distinct tasks: identifying the emitter count $N$ and estimating their positions $\left\{x^{i}\right\}$. Existing fit-and-select frameworks fit the measured intensity and autocorrelation data using several models corresponding to different values of $N$ and then select the best-supported model. This procedure lets errors from the multi-parameter optimization of emitter positions propagate into the choice of model, degrading performance under photon-limited and high-background conditions. We propose a method that directly infers the emitter count and positions from the multimodal data via learned inference. Learned inference improves both the emitter-counting accuracy and localization precision compared to the fit-and-select method. It achieves more than tenfold improvement in precision and requires up to five times fewer photons to achieve practically meaningful localization with the largest gains observed under lo

papers.title: Freeform gradient-index media reconstruction
papers.abs: Reconstructing a gradient-index (GRIN) medium consists of determining a spatial refractive index distribution that produces a prescribed ray trajectory, an inverse problem in geometrical optics. Previous approaches have used geometrical symmetries and conserved ray quantities to address this inverse problem. Extending reconstruction to freeform media requires approaches that do not rely on these symmetries. Here, we present a three-dimensional point-wise method for reconstructing freeform GRIN media through the inverse application of local refraction. The method does not require geometrical symmetry, paraxial approximations, or prior knowledge of the iso-indicial surfaces, and is straightforward to implement. Reconstruction using two interface geometries demonstrates that different refractive index distributions can be obtained from the same prescribed trajectory function. The choice of interfaces thus provides an additional degree of freedom for optical design, subject to local refraction conditions and compatibility between overlapping reconstructed regions.

papers.abs: Optical frequency combs have transformed molecular spectroscopy by enabling broadband, high-resolution analysis, yet they are conventionally used as light sources to interrogate external samples. Gaseous analytes interact directly with the evanescent field of light recirculating within the resonator, enhancing sensitivity while encoding analyte-induced perturbations across the microcomb's collective spectral response. Rather than relying on a single optical resonance, we exploit distributed responses across multiple comb lines to generate multidimensional molecular fingerprints. Adding more comb lines systematically improves analyte discrimination, showing that the microcomb provides sensing information beyond what individual spectral channels offer. papers.title: Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
papers.abs: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.

papers.abs: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. papers.abs: The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. However, orbital angular momentum (OAM) is increasingly recognized as a more direct electronic response to molecular chirality. A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals. The model incorporates major minor groove asymmetry, an axial base pair offset representing stagger, and compositional inequivalence between the two strands, providing structural control parameters with which the orbital response can be tuned. papers.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
papers.abs: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. Noise suppression of quantum frequency conversion in thin-film lithium niobate waveguides via adapted poling
papers.abs: Quantum frequency conversion (QFC) enables optical interfaces between dissimilar quantum systems, but suppressing noise while maintaining high conversion efficiency remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that adapted poling in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguides reduces the pump-power requirement while shifting the dominant noise mechanism and its power scaling. In 2-cm-long waveguides, adapted poling enables maximum conversion efficiency at an on-chip pump power of $19\pm0.8$~mW, reducing the required pump power by 8~dB and the total conversion noise by 14~dB relative to conventional periodic poling at their respective maximum-conversion operating points. Controlled measurements with different pump conditions and device configurations reveal a transition from predominantly quadratic noise scaling in periodically poled devices to predominantly linear scaling in adapted-poling devices. papers.abs: The realization of artificial magnetic structures with high epitaxial quality and elevated critical temperatures remains a key challenge for spintronics. Here, we report the fabrication and characterization of epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures grown by layer-by-layer laser ablation. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, magnetization measurements, and neutron diffraction confirm their exceptional crystalline order and the absence of structural defects. Neutron diffraction reveals no antiferromagnetic at non-zero wavevector Bragg peaks, ruling out most antiferromagnetic configurations with a non zero wave vector Q. Magnetic hysteresis loops instead evidence a ferromagnetic order with a remanent moment of about 0.5 Bohr magneton per Mn atom at room temperature, persisting either in-plane or out-of-plane depending on the applied field. A compact, dual-colour chirped-pulse laser system for field-deployable coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering diagnostics
papers.abs: Single-shot coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering (CRBS) requires dual colour, frequency, and pulse duration agile laser systems, currently available only in laboratory layouts. In this work, we present a compact, portable, and robust next generation laser system that meets all of these requirements. Key features include an integrated master-slave seed laser design for stable frequency chirping, fiber-coupled acousto-optic modulator (AOM) gated pulse shaping for long-term thermal stability, and customized amplification stages in a rugged, portable enclosure which simplifiy the alignment and maintenance process. The system in this implementation can deliver up to $450$~mJ per arm, chirp rates up to $\sim22$~MHz$/$ns, and arbitrary temporal profiles within $\sim25$~ns to $\sim1$~$μ$s. This laser system is validated by measuring the neutral number density of an atmospheric plasma jet, and a two-dimensional temperature map is constructed, demonstrating lab-grade diagnostics for field deployment.

A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Source of Broadband Polarisation-Entangled Photon Pairs at Telecom Wavelengths using Zn-indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides
papers.abs: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Operating across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum using pump-suppression filtering only, the source exhibits a measured bandwidth of approximately 67 nm. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.

papers.abs: We extend our previous study of squeezed two-component Schrödinger cat states to a phase-referenced single-mode family with an arbitrary number $N$ of coherent components and general relative phases. Within the established circular-state construction, we derive a closed complex overlap kernel for the ordered action of displacement, phase rotation, and squeezing, retaining exact finite-amplitude normalization. We distinguish finite-displacement orthogonality from local phase-estimation sensitivity quantified by quantum Fisher information (QFI). For equal-phase states, we compare $N=2,\ldots,9$ at a common mean photon number and include coherent-state and squeezed-vacuum benchmarks. A bound on the higher photon-number sectors establishes the fixed-energy asymptote $F_{Q,N}=4\bar n(N-\bar n)+o(1)$. Its leading term agrees with the known QFI of a vacuum--$N$-photon superposition. Surveying Experimentally-Validated Components for DNA-Based Molecular Communication
papers.abs: Molecular communication is a novel paradigm for the design of nanonetworks. It uses molecules as information carriers and enables communication between nanodevices. DNA-based molecular communication is a promising approach for medical applications, such as in-body networks for diagnostics and drug delivery. However, the transition from theoretical models to practical experiments is still in its early stages. This survey reviews experimentally validated DNA-tiles, nanocarriers, and biosensors relevant to implementing DNA-tile-based nanonetworks in vitro. We evaluate these components based on their stability, compatibility, cost-effectiveness, and overall suitability for wet-lab implementation. Based on this analysis, we identify promising component combinations and derive a blueprint for a minimal proof-of-concept experiment. The resulting framework provides researchers with both a structured overview of experimentally relevant design choices and a concrete starting point for implementing and validating DNA-based nanonetworks in the wet lab.

papers.title: Kinematics of Inverse Compton Scattering from Dirac Carriers in Graphene
papers.abs: We examine the kinematics of Compton and inverse Compton scattering by Dirac carriers in graphene. Unlike photons in vacuum, which propagate at the speed of light c, graphene carriers have a characteristic velocity vF, with vF much less than c. This difference means that the standard Compton scattering formula cannot be applied to graphene simply by replacing c with vF. We first examine Compton-like scattering for a gapless Dirac carrier initially at the Dirac point and for a gapped carrier at the band edge, both corresponding to zero in-plane momentum. We then consider scattering from an energetic gapless Dirac carrier. By combining energy conservation with the graphene dispersion and in-plane momentum conservation, we obtain a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy within the model considered. This relation is the main kinematic result of the work. We identify inverse Compton-like scattering by the transfer of energy from the carrier to the photon, subject to the simultaneous conservation of energy and in-plane momentum. Wavelength Diversity Expands the Expressive Power of Optical Computing
papers.abs: Universal function approximation underpins neural networks' capacity to represent nonlinear relationships, but realizing this capability in optical hardware requires engineering the computational features encoded in light. Here, we show that wavelength diversity enhances optical function-approximation expressivity through wavelength-scaled Fourier features generated by a shared phase encoder, without increasing the number of input-encoded harmonics. papers.abs: Conservative nonlinear waves generally undergo an irreversible process of thermalization toward the Rayleigh--Jeans (RJ) equilibrium state. Light thermalization has recently been experimentally investigated in the two-dimensional transverse spatial dynamics of multimode waveguides. Here, we consider the one-dimensional temporal dynamics of incoherent light propagating in a weakly birefringent single-mode fiber. papers.abs: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. papers.abs: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding $F > 0.99$, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.

papers.abs: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference underpins many photonic quantum information protocols and is commonly characterized by a single visibility parameter. This quantity is typically obtained by averaging over a fixed coincidence window, thereby discarding details of the underlying temporal structure that are critical in continuous-wave processes. Four-photon interference with continuous-wave sources furthermore requires photon pairs with long coherence times, which we generate in microring resonators and measure with ultrafast time-resolved detection. Here, we model and resolve their interference and temporal structure by recording all four photon arrival times and mapping their relative delays onto a three-dimensional coincidence histogram relative to a trigger detection. The resulting structure preserves relative arrival-time correlations that are usually discarded and enables post-processed optimization of coincidence windows to trade off visibility against count rate. This method provides a general benchmark for continuous-wave sources in interference-based quantum network protocols.
